title: Robotic partial nephrectomy
subtitle: Short clamp, clear margin, two-layer renorrhaphy

sources.title: EAU Guidelines on Renal Cell Carcinoma
BAUS procedure-specific patient information and consent guidance

indications: A localised renal tumour (usually T1) where removing only the tumour keeps kidney function, especially with a solitary kidney or reduced function.
contraindications: Tumour too large or central to remove safely with margin.
Unfit for surgery (active surveillance or ablation instead).
preparation: Contrast CT or MRI; complexity score (for example RENAL); chest imaging.
Renal function and split function if needed.
Consent: bleeding and transfusion, urine leak, conversion to radical nephrectomy, positive margin.
positioning: Flank position about 60 degrees, padded, strapped, table flexed.
equipment: Robot, intraoperative ultrasound probe, bulldog clamps, sliding-clip renorrhaphy sutures, haemostatic agents, retrieval bag.
anatomy: Renal artery and its branches, renal vein, collecting system, the tumour and its depth.
criticalSafety: Record warm ischaemia; aim for under about 25 minutes.
Close the collecting system and any opened vessels.
commonErrors: A missed accessory artery and bleeding on excision.
complications: Bleeding (early or late from a pseudoaneurysm).
postop: Late bleeding or haematuria: think pseudoaneurysm and angiography.

steps.emphasis: Imaging, complexity score and the plan for a solitary or normal kidney reviewed.
Flank position about 60 degrees, padded and strapped, table flexed.
Hilar or parenchymal bleeding: press, tell the anaesthetist, add a port or convert; consider clamping again.
Tumour in a bag, out intact.
With the pneumoperitoneum lowered, check the renorrhaphy and the hilum.
Record warm ischaemia time, collecting system entry and repair, and margins seen.

step.pn.hilum.title: Expose and control the hilum
step.pn.hilum.why: The artery must be controlled before the tumour is cut. Every artery is found, because a missed branch bleeds during excision.
how: Reflect the colon, find the ureter and gonadal vein and follow them up to the hilum.
Dissect the renal artery (and any accessory arteries) and the vein; place vessel loops.
Compare the arteries found with the CT.

step.pn.ultrasound.title: Ultrasound and score the margin
step.pn.ultrasound.why: The tumour's deep edge is not visible. Ultrasound shows its depth and outline so the cut keeps a rim of normal kidney.
how: Defat the kidney around the tumour, keeping the fat over the tumour.
Scan with the intraoperative probe to see the tumour edge and depth.
Score a line with cautery a few millimetres outside the edge.
pitfalls: Scoring too close and entering the tumour.

step.pn.clamp.title: Clamp the artery and start the clock
step.pn.clamp.why: Clamping makes the field bloodless. Warm ischaemia beyond about 25 to 30 minutes adds to kidney damage.
how: Tell the anaesthetist; give mannitol if used locally.
Place bulldog clamps on the artery (and accessory arteries); clamp the vein only if needed.
Start a timer called aloud at intervals.
pitfalls: Incomplete clamping and a bloody field.

step.pn.excise.title: Excise the tumour with a rim
step.pn.excise.why: A thin rim of normal kidney around the tumour gives a clear margin without wasting kidney.
how: Cut along the scored line with cold scissors, following the tumour's curve.
Keep a thin layer of normal kidney on the tumour all round; open the collecting system if needed.
Put the tumour aside in the abdomen for the bag.

step.pn.renorrhaphy.title: Two-layer renorrhaphy
step.pn.renorrhaphy.why: The inner layer closes opened vessels and the collecting system; the outer layer brings the kidney edges together and stops bleeding.
how: Inner layer: running absorbable suture along the base, closing the collecting system and open vessels.
Outer layer: interrupted or sliding-clip sutures across the defect, tightened without cutting through.
Haemostatic agent in the bed if used.
pitfalls: Sutures that cut through the parenchyma.

step.pn.unclamp.title: Unclamp and record the warm time
step.pn.unclamp.why: The kidney must pink up and stop bleeding. The warm ischaemia time is part of the operation note.
how: Remove the bulldogs and call the warm ischaemia time aloud.
Watch the kidney reperfuse and the renorrhaphy for bleeding; add sutures as needed.
Record the time in the note.
